建议靠近这个恒星系的话一定要小心点。

texts.en:
We have lost communication with our science ship [this.GetName] in [cutholoid_under_radar.solar_system.GetName].

Their last transmission indicated they were beginning a survey on a nearby asteroid, [cutholoid_under_radar.GetName].

Caution is advised when re-entering this system.

texts.zh: [cutholoid_under_radar.GetName]小行星不可貌相。我们需要派遣一支小有规模的军队前去，在[this.GetName]科研船永远离开我们之前将其救出。
texts.en: The asteroid [cutholoid_under_radar.GetName] is not what it seems to be. We should approach with a sizable military force and attempt to recover our science ship [this.GetName] before it is gone for good.

sections.zh: 轨道上有$COUNT$/$REQUIRED$支战斗力至少为600的舰队。
sections.en: Has $COUNT$/$REQUIRED$ fleet(s) with at least 600 fleet power in orbit.

texts.zh: [from.GetName]的应急通讯戛然而止。我们只能相信[from.GetName]科研船已经永远离我们而去了。
texts.en: The emergency transmissions from [from.GetName] have ceased. We can only assume the science ship [from.GetName] has been lost for good.

title.en: From the Belly of the Beast

texts.zh:
我们在[current_system.GetName]失踪的科研船回来了！

[leader.GetName]发回的报道称，他们被一个藏在小行星中的太空实体整个吞下，最后在船体就要承受不住的时候意外地被吐了出来。似乎有什么别的东西把这个生物吓了一跳让我们侥幸逃脱。

在有更多的认知之前，探索这片小行星带可要多加小心了。
texts.en:
Our Science Ship lost in [current_system.GetName] has returned!

Reports have come in from [leader.GetName] that they had been swallowed whole by a spaceborne entity hiding inside of an asteroid, and were at the limits of hull integrity before being unexpectedly ejected to safety. It appears something else has surprised the creature before we could intervene.

We should be cautious in our approach of certain asteroid belts until we can learn more.

texts.zh: [cutholoid_under_radar.GetName]小行星不可貌相。我们有了合适的科技，可以将其整个捕获并在[this.GetName]永远离开我们之前将其轻易地救出。
texts.en: The asteroid [cutholoid_under_radar.GetName] is not what it seems to be. With the right technology, we could capture it entirely and easily recover our science ship [this.GetName] before it is gone for good.

texts.zh:
[fromfrom.GetName]中的小行星只是一只栖居在里面的巨大有机体的外壳。

我们成功地将其摧毁，并找回了[this.GetName]。此后调查小行星的时候可得小心了。

可能还有其他的这种生物潜藏于此，等待着不小心的猎物。不幸的是，[leader.GetName]遭受到了一些不可修复的损伤。
texts.en:
The asteroid in [fromfrom.GetName] served only as a shell for a massive organism living inside.

We have successfully destroyed it and recovered [this.GetName]. Caution should be taken in further investigations of asteroids.

More of these creatures may be out there, lying in wait of easy prey. Unfortunately, [leader.GetName] suffered some irreparable harm.

texts.en:
The asteroid in [fromfrom.GetName] served only as a shell for a massive organism living inside.

We have successfully destroyed it and recovered [this.GetName]. Caution should be taken in further investigations of asteroids.

More of these creatures may be out there, lying in wait of easy prey.

texts.zh:
我们发现了一种居住在小行星外壳内的太空生物，将其命名为岩居兽。它们是一种可以埋伏数年只为给猎物致命一击的伏击掠食者。它们极度危险，能吞下整艘舰船，所以在探索那些未调查的小行星带时务必格外小心。

好消息是，它们的数量非常稀少，而且无性繁殖流程可能要花费上百年。
texts.en:
We have discovered a spaceborne organism that shelters inside of asteroids. Known to us as "Cutholoids", these creatures are ambush predators that are capable of lying in wait for several years to capture their prey. Capable of engulfing entire ships, we should be very careful when approaching unsurveyed asteroid belts as they are found to be extremely dangerous.

The good news is that they appear to be quite rare, and their asexual reproductive processes can take hundreds of years.

texts.zh: 我们认为这些生物会根据大小和矿物成分来选择用哪颗小星星来作为巢穴。虽然我们遇到的第一个样本对[GetCommonMineral]具有生物学偏好，但每个个体很可能随着时间的推移根据其当前环境发展出不同的适应性。扫描显示这种金属的痕迹遍布宿主小行星，以及“岩居兽”本身的神经系统和消化道。
texts.en: We believe that the creatures select their asteroids based on mineral composition as well as size. While the first specimen we encountered possesses a biological preference for [GetCommonMineral], it is likely each individual develops this adaptation over time based on their current environment. Scans show that traces of this metal are present throughout the host asteroid, as well as within the nervous system and digestive tract of the "Cutholoid" Itself.

label.zh: 我们应该进一步研究这些生物。
label.en: We should study these creatures further.

label.zh: 伏击猎食者吗。全部摧毁。
伏击猎食者吗。全部摧毁。

texts.zh: 岩居兽的小行星外壳是一件令人印象深刻的生物工程杰作。我们还有很多可以向它们学习的。
texts.en: The asteroidal shell structure of the Cutholoid is an impressive piece of biological engineering. There is more for us to learn from them.

texts.zh:
岩居兽的外壳并不只是矿物而已，其中还有生物纤维补强。这些纤维一直都在生长，这种外壳中估计包含了超过一半的生物质。

当岩居兽长得住不下小行星时，他们会寻找下一个新家并再次开始整合流程。虽然它们通常具有很强的领地意识，但在极佳的外壳候选品的轨道上也会出现多只岩居兽，其中最大的一只将占据这颗新的小行星，而其他个体将按大小排序，和平地交换外壳。通过这种方式，它们居住的小行星往往会交换十几手之多。

最终的结果是，最小的小行星会因为交换频繁反而得到了最多的生物强化。这些样品具有重要的科学价值。
texts.en:
The shell of a Cutholoid is not mineral alone, but reinforced with strong biological fibers. These fibers never stop growing, and the composition of some shells is estimated to be over fifty percent biomass.

When a Cutholoid grows too large for its asteroid, it will seek another home and begin the integration process again. While they are normally highly territorial, multiple Cutholoids have been observed in orbit of a prime shell candidate. The largest of the creatures will occupy the fresh asteroid, while others will order themselves by size and peacefully swap with the next in line. In this way, the asteroids they inhabit have often been occupied by dozens of previous organisms.

The end result is that the smallest asteroids have the highest amount of biological reinforcement, as they have been exchanged most often. These samples contain significant scientific value.

texts.zh:
我们的一艘科研船在[cutholoid_under_radar.solar_system.GetName]调查一颗奇怪的小行星时失去了联系。

在他们最后失踪的地点探测到了微弱的应急信号，我如果要找回这艘失踪的舰船就需要进一步调查。
texts.en:
Contact has been lost with our Science Ship while investigating a strange asteroid in [cutholoid_under_radar.solar_system.GetName].

We are detecting weak emergency signals from their last known location, and should investigate further if we intend to recover the missing vessel.

texts.zh:
在[from.solar_system.GetName]进行例行探索的过程中发现了另一个奇怪的小行星状生物。

我们应该避免让科研船接近这个星系，直到我们对这个危险的物体有更多的了解为止。
texts.en:
Another of the strange asteroidal creatures have been discovered in [from.solar_system.GetName] during routine exploration.

We should avoid this system with our Science Ships until we know more about these dangerous objects.
